To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) a general static analysis framework for Android apps can be built with a few hundred lines of code, (b) the framework can be used to build specialized analyses for security vetting with a similar number of additional lines of code, which is much less than the number of lines of code in the existing tools, and (c), when the same set of problems is addressed, the results from the specialized analyses built with the framework are at least on par with the results of the existing specialized analyses

we have built a new framework called Amandroids for static security vetting of android apps that (1) can perform comprehensive inter-component analysis of an Android app, (2) can be used to build a variety of specialized security analyses with little additional coding, and (3) can achieve the same level of precision as prior specialized works and often exceeds their precision.

(i) the static analysis for security problems in mobile apps is not as intractable as one might think; (ii) one can easily build various specialized analyses on top of a general analysis, and the resulting specialized analyses can be as effective or more effective than those designed specifically for the problem; and (iii) Amandroid is an effective and efficient general framework for building specialized analyses for vetting Android apps.

the following question: how to build a general and precise framework for static analysis of Android apps, and how to leverage the result of such a general analysis to build specialized analyses to address various security problems of Android apps.
